item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse
item.content:encoded:
Excellent, excellent; thank you for clarifying. This is shaping up real well.

Responding to a conversation that occurred in PMs, I still believe the "middle" of the story you've got is a little lacking. Ideally you would want to fill it with primary evidence taken from the premises of her previous holders, such as a convenient journal entry (either documenting someone's personal thoughts or, more ideally, "containment procedures" and incident reports). This could be followed by a Foundation incident report of some kind, which would highlight the malevolent intent of the reflections.

I also still take issue with this end-of-article twist being revealed in an interview room, given upon being asked for it nicely. There should be something in the way of the audience learning this information that, when it's overcome, is satisfying. I'd imagine this would be as simple as having her be non-responsive to questioning, and then reveals the information to a researcher after some big event occurs (that aforementioned incident report, perhaps?). I'm imagining a scene of the girl and a researcher standing in front of a mirror in her containment chamber, when she suddenly begins to speak to them — the imagery, at least, is more varied than a mundane interview room.

This execution would require you to really nail the feeling of dread that should be emanating from these reflection people, to make them seem like a good thread. Does any of that sound interesting?

item.title: Re: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
Gotta start off by saying, I’m generally a fan of all things fae (I mean, just look at my profile picture). So I like the idea of a fairy-based SCP. Though I’m noticing a few things here that I have to question.

First, what’s with the symmetrical hole? It just seems random and it’s never really explained. You seem to have such a consistent them with the traits later, and then there’s just this at the beginning. Second, is this actually fairies or is it just fairy-like? Either answer is fine but you want your reader to understand which it is. Because if I were reading this I’d think “cool, a forest that makes people go insane” not “there are probably creatures in that forest”. So if you actually want to be using fairies you should probably have some appear, but if you just want to use the traits of fairies and attribute them to a forest that’s also an option.

I’m going to throw out a suggestion, and keep in mind that you by no means have to take this. But you might want to write this as a tale. After all it doesn’t seem like you’re that interested in the containment of this anomaly. You didn’t even touch on that in your pitch. I could see a tale that was entirely devoted to the task force exploring this forest. It would give us more of a view into how they’re reacting to all the chaos happening around them. Again, I’m just throwing that out there. This can still work perfectly fine as a regular article.

item.title: Re: So Let It Be Written, So Let It Be Done
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the Feedback
Hide Reply

Thanks, Dankaar,

I appreciate the feedback, first and foremost. The reverse approach, seeing the unaffected astronauts as the affected, is fascinating. Lots of potential for "containment" by keeping an eye on earth-bound events by comparing them to a non-earth-bound control.

In my drafts, neither of the original holders of the stone ever realize that the stone is the cause of the anomalous events. With all the tools that are used, the new location, the impracticality of testing individual books and tools, they're simply unable to pinpoint the source. Hence the frustration and the eventual unravelling of their characters.

Also, in my drafts (I'm writing this story out long form for NaNoWriMo), the SCP's effects are limited to the event itself (raising Atlantis from a repaired book on Greek Mythology), and public perception of the event. Centuries of evidence concluding that Atlantis was an allegory invented by Plato to make a point still exist unchanged. People can and occasionally do come across this evidence but, as the ultimate confirmation bias, they assume that it's all flawed or incorrect because they just know the place is real. In the long form, the protagonists realize that they know both realities are true before remembering that they'd set up a test to change a particular outcome. The SCP doesn't rewrite history, really, it just changes our perception of it, and so the physical changes are accepted as reality.

I too was struggling with how the Foundation gets in on this, but I really love the "reverse effect" perspective which alerts them to Foundation-level weirdness, after which they trace the effects back to stone… somehow. I was tempted to throw an MC&D reference in with the antique store, perhaps the Foundation was tracking this artifact without knowing its effects, and the investigations merge.

Thank you again for the feedback and ideas!

item.title: Re: SCP Concept: Reflection
item.content:encoded:
Hey, thank you for the feedback, I'll be sure to answer your questions! Ok, the gas station doesn't have any custom unique features to it, it's a normal gas station that you would find on the road, sometimes it can adapt to it's area to make it more natural but it's pretty much just an ordinary gas station.

It's mostly the same usually, the products are only changed if they don't exist or aren't really common in the area and the prices are the normal price the product would have. The gas station's shape will always stay the same.

The area doesn't really matter much, the SCP only moves itself to places where it's target will go by and stop to take a quick break, but it's obvious it can only appear somewhere where it fits, it can't just appear randomly inside of a building.

The Foundation didn't of course know at first this was a gas station SCP that murdered the Staff member, but they were aware of the possibility of an SCP, so after that the Foundation started sending Field Agents to investigate on anomalies that could be happening. After gathering more info, Staff members started theorizing on it's containment and later would successfully contain it by having 4 or 5 guards take shifts to stay and secure the area so no anomaly occurs and the gas station moves somewhere or the mirror affects anyone.

I will take those into account, I really do appreciate your thoughts and if any more questions or ideas come up tell me, thank you.

item.title: Re: So Let It Be Written, So Let It Be Done
item.content:encoded:
So, my question is this: does this SCP affect the relevant records on Earth anytime the SCP does its thing?

If so, you could attack this from the opposite angle: the SCP Foundation initially belives the SCP to be an event that affects sattleites and astronauts, ocasionally implanting both with fake memories or data about Earth, when what is really happening is the stone thing. The sattleites and astronauts are unaffected because the effects of the SCP are strictly Earthbound.

From there, you could then work your way to the narrative you had planned (perhaps the SCP being from a seperate investigation initially unrelated to the sattleite phenomenon?) I suggest this because, as-is, it would be difficult for the Foundation to "naturally" learn of this SCP's existence, and you've kinda-sorta created a plot hole by having the book binders suspect that the SCP is causing the stuff despite its effects on humanity's perception of history. Having them chase down the effects (even if they're incorrect) feels like a better way.

Also burning the bookstore in-universe is a bit much if the intent was to destroy the SCP. Sledgehammer or dropping it from a high place would've been the smater move for the guys.

item.title: the man in the corner
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Page Layout: Class, containment procedures, how it was found, tests run on it.
Elevator Pitch: Easy way to put it is the SCP looks like an average old man except he is always facing the corner of a room facing magnetic north at midnight and every two hours moves to another corner. His face is always in shadow nothing can be done to see it or probe it. He must always be kept in a perfectly square room made of concrete with an aggregate of bone and seashell one of the few objects he cannot destroy. The walls must be perfectly smooth any cracks or chips in the wall causes the SCP to react and turn the room back to a perfect square. The SCP does this by creating a black shadow around itself that engulfs the room no light can enter this shadow and any who enter are turned to bone and blood. Once the shadow vanishes the room is perfectly square once again though slightly bigger.
Central Narrative: The initial discovery of the SCP in Canada comes first along with a new mobile task force called the Canada goose. The next is an incident involving a chip in the wall and the SCP’s reaction then two files hidden by 05 council. Then a new test which gives a hint to removed files and finally placing the SCP in a perfectly round room. Followed by a major incident report that explains what happened in the missing reports.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: There is more to the SCP than what we see it is hinted he knows foundation secrets. How he kills and changes his room size is unknown as nobody who entered his holding cell during an event has lived and no residue, but bone and blood can be found. There is also the mystery about what this SCP knows and why it scares the higher-ups in the foundation.
Additional Notes: I got into SCP a few months ago and I really wanted to write my own and hope people come to enjoy it.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlights: My Eyes are Up Here
item.content:encoded:
Sorry for any misinterpretation I may have caused! I chalk this partially up to my not knowing how much information I should be putting into these posts, lest it come across as too long, causing no one to read it.

Thank you for giving me the opportunity to clarify my stance, which I will do now: This is 100% NOT supposed to be a "haha boob" joke. I now understand how my juxtaposition of the word "comedy" with this piece (which is, indeed, intended to be an anti-harassment tale) caused confusion; the part that I viewed as humorous was the fate of the lecher who, as a result of his inability to quit ogling, was ultimately forced to do so.

A detail I omitted from my brief description that perhaps would have helped me better express my true intentions, one which I do plan to include in the finished piece, should I write it, is that during experimentation, the carved possessive word which seemingly appears on her body is observed to come from no one and nowhere but the SCP itself (i.e. there is no "other being" out there causing it): it is an act of self-claiming, of saying "Lay off; this isn't yours to stare at".

Speaking of testing, almost all of the test data and containment procedure will, of course, be conducted with Dr. Lopez's full consent and within her comfort bounds. While the SCP is identified as its own separate entity, there is still the sense of it being her body, allowing her primary jurisdiction over it (there's a reason I made the "host" an SCP researcher, meaning that she can be in control of and report most of the data herself).

I acknowledge and agree with your aside - I had failed to take the publication date into reference - and to answer the hypothetical question at the end, yes, I think I am capable of composing this piece in a way that it does not come off as a joke about the female anatomy, but rather as a respectful commentary on harassment with a twist of sweet vengeance towards misogynists. I will be sure to be careful with my wording and have several people check over it prior to anywhere near potential publication.

With all that in mind, I would be absolutely thrilled if you could read through this again with this new context and provide further commentary! If not, I have already taken up plenty of your time discussing these matters. Thank you yet again for talking this through with me!!

item.title: Re: SCP Concept: Reflection
item.content:encoded:
DISCLAIMER: I am a newbie and I can't give green-lights.
Take my advice with a large grain of salt.

I'm leaving this here temporarily, I shall add critique below this as soon as I am able to.

Ello there! So there's quite a bit I really enjoy about this, and then there is some stuff I'd like to give advice on.

I'll start off with what I thought was really good about this concept.

1. I really love how your SCP is setup, it's simple and to the point. It makes it really easy to come across and understand.

2. I also really like the concept, it's one that can lead to a lot when it comes to storytelling of the Foundation staff or people around the SCP. The fact that the SCP moves between different places with not many restrictions means that your story is not constrained from one part physical world. This means you can add lore and interviews revolving around the SCP from multiple different places. Heck, I'd say go one step further and add some wackiness in there. If the SCP isn't restricted to being in a place like a city, have one of the reported locations that it was found in be something crazy like in the middle of a uninhabited desert.

Now I do have some things I'd like to address that I'm quite confused on.

1. Try being more specific about how the SCP operates. I especially think you need to give some more detail into the "gas station" part of the SCP itself.

  • What kind of gas station is it? Is it of a specific custom brand or does it change randomly between other gas station brands to help its manipulation?
  • Does the gas station change its products, shape, and pricing based on where it's located or is it the same no matter where it is?
  • Does the SCP have any restrictions to where it changes its location? Can it appear in any part of the world or does it only spawn in areas like cities and common gas-station locations? I get that you described in the findings that the SCP was "never there before" according to the staff researcher, but you got to give more detail into where it "moves between places".

2. How does the Foundation know about these findings? According to your story, the body of the staff member was found, but that doesn't describe to the Foundation what exactly happened.

  • If the Foundation can't find the gas station (since it moves after the mirror is shattered) how does the Foundation know that the staff member was even killed by an anomalous entity?

I recommend giving more explanation into this. Here's some ideas I can give:

  • Have the Foundation ask other staff in the local area of any sudden changes.
  • Have the Foundation spot a correlation between multiple discoveries of the same kind of events.

EDIT: Sorry for typos and bad syntax, I was using a phone earlier when reviewing this.

item.title: Re: SCP Concept: Reflection
item.content:encoded:
Disclaimer: I am a newbie and cannot grant you greenlight.

Hey there, Cesss. The idea itself is pretty unique, if nothing else. I've been following the SCP Foundation for a couple of years and I don't think I ever read about a Gas station being an SCP before. I could also see a couple possible options for a good interview being made out of the narrative you have provided, which is always nice to see.

Now, I would have a question, if I may: does this SCP seek out Foundation personnel to make into it's victims on it's own? Because while I know that Foundation personnel are the most likely to die at the hands of SCPs, I find it peculiar in your article.

You said the Researcher was driving home from work, meaning he was leaving a Site or Facility of the Foundation. I would be of the opinion that the Foundation keeps a good patrol around their Facilities, taking in consideration what they work with.

Next, you said that this SCP swaps the real person with the reflection. I take it then, that the Researcher was trapped in a pocket dimension within the mirror, looking at the reflection which was now controlling his body? Then, if they both swung a hammer at each other, which can only inflict bludgeoning wounds, why did the Research die of multiple lacerations?

Another question I would have: how would this SCP be contained?

Lastly, there are a couple of SCPs with reflection as their main selling point on the side. Currently I can think of SCP-125, and SCP-1620. As the author of your SCP, you know the exact details to your article, so I would recommend you looking up any other SCPs like 125 and 1620 and check for similarities, in order to avoid your article being too similar to already existing ones.

With that said, I kind of really like your article here. With a bit of fine-tuning and a bit more highlight into the swapping process, I could see this getting somewhere.

Again, please remember that I am a newbie. Take everything I said with a grain of salt.

item.title: Re: A Day in the Life *Seeking Greenlights*

I think there could really be something here. The balance between finances and ethical dilemma is something that I think could easily serve to dramatize very real problems that are going on in the world today, especially if you are the kind of person that keeps up with that kind of thing. There's a space to play in that this creates for a whole range of possibilities.

I will say that I'm hesitant towards the inclusion of existing articles. Not to say that they don't belong in the space (they by all means do), but I think making up scenarios of your own could allow for more flexibility in forming the kind of impact you intend for the article. The Containment Psychiatry Orientation does that towards the end to great effectiveness, using a globally known creature, the vampire, as an example to punctuate a unique kind of cruelty.

All in all, I feel some real gold in this. Consider this a greenlight.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlights: My Eyes are Up Here
item.content:encoded:
Upon retrospect, I think there was a fair amount of misinterpretation involved with the original post. I'd like to take a moment to reaffirm your stance, and what you hope to achieve with this article.

I'm visualizing two different interpretations in my head, both formed from your reply and the content of original post. You wanted to make this a comedy, which stuck to me as problematic. If you wanted to tell an anti-harassment story involving the objectification of women, making it comedy based spoke as an intense clashing of themes, and a desire to make this a "haha boobs" joke, which is where my original dissent came from.

If this is to be a protest against the type of behavior outlined in the original post, then that's completely different. As I said, how much comedy is it that you want, or indeed, how much is healthy for this type of story? My question stands as not what frivolous changes might make this work, but rather the bigger picture.

As an aside, 1004 was written in 2011, back when site standards and ediquette were different. I don't want you to just ask yourself "is this okay to write?", I want you to ask yourself "am I able to write this in a respectful, sensible manner while still conveying the story I wish to tell?"

item.title: SCP Concept: The Dream Zombies (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking-Greenlights: Yes

Page-Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page-Layout: Default SCP-Layout

Elevator-Pitch:

SCP-XXXX is a small patterned child's bed that emits a comforting attraction-aura of childhood and nostalgia. The bed makes any entity that sleeps in it have nightmares of green-glowing zombies attempting to eat their stomach. In dreams, people "get out of bed" in their current/old household (sometimes-combined).

After sleeping in the SCP, the user will have these nightmares every-time they go to sleep anywhere.
When having nightmares, people suddenly wake up in a panicked-state, which causes sleep deprivation. Some experience PTSD.

If multiple people feel the attraction of the SCP, all shall get aggressive at one-another and fight until one remains/all die. Aura-attraction to SCP is instant ONLY in a 10-feet radius to the SCP, and ONLY goes away for 9-to-15-minutes after awakening from it.

+ READ MORE
- READ LESS

Central-Narrative:

SCP-XXXX was found by Field-Agent, Chris, in Florida when investigating multiple reports of "eeriness" of an abandoned hospital from locals. Agent-C, under SCPs attraction-affect, realized the affect and called for backup. Three other Field-Agents arrived (with recording hardware) and found Agent-C sleeping in the SCP. All agents felt the affect of SCP, ending with a fight between the four agents where Agent-K killed all three other agents with a pistol and slept in the SCP.

Mobile Task Force Psi-7 was called in by Agent-K after waking up and leaving, which all twenty MTF were not able to contain the SCP due its attraction force. MTF member, Cadet-F, survived bloodshed and reported the incident after sleeping.

Agent-K and Cadet-F were taken into investigation with recorded evidence/interviews of what occurred.
Both were carefully watched over in-study by research staff, where Foundation realized consistent nightmares.
Both were given amnesics and therapy all which only helped endurance with the-nightmares and trauma. (SCP-500-use blocked by 05-council for scarcity-issues)

Agent-K was also questioned in later dates/interviews to describe any further issues he experienced (such as nightmares).

The SCP is left in the abandoned-building, guarded by 10 undercover guards looking like U.S-police to ensure locals don't enter.
Only researchers/needed-personnel are allowed inside.

D-Class studies/interviews/experiments and small-animal research confirmed SCP's affects like nightmares, aura-attraction, PTSD, and sleep deprivation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

Based on real nightmares I had as a kid after playing the game "Nicktoons Unite!".

Unlike other Bed-SCPs, it anomaly/nightmares "sticks" to its users.

Story is short-&-sweet.

item.title: Re: Hephaestus - SCP Concept
item.content:encoded:
My biggest question here is how is this linked to Hephestus at all?

Hephestus is the greek god of fire, true, but he's better known as the god of metalworking and forges, in addition to fire, stone masonry, and sculpture. A random forest fire in Norway seems to be an odd thing for Hephestus to be interested in/namedropped unless he's filling in for Logi for some reason (a fire giant from Norse mythology who appears to act as the personification of fire; he beat Loki once in a competition).

Now, if this was a fire in Greece, and the area around it was called something like "Forge of Olympus" or somesuch, then namedropping Hephestus might be more appropriate.

Outside of that, I feel this is a hard sell as-is. The fire can't be put out, so what? Your central narrative as-described is basically "here's how it was found and what its doing." There's little beyond that, no real indication of greater powers at play, sapiance on part of the SCP, or anything beyond "neverending forest fire" and, as described, no indication of a "man vs the worst of mother nature" drama. It's… just a normal wildfire, albiet one that you can't put out.

Is there something I missed, or did you have more going on under the hood than what you wrote here?

item.title: Greenlight request: Tattooed hydraulic press
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes
Page type: SCP Article

First of all sorry for my repost. I didn't get any greenlights or the amount of feedback I had hoped for. Also I'm new to the wiki so I don't know the proper channels.

The SCP is already written by me and is currently residing in my sandbox until I get enough greenlights to get the SCP reviewed.

Elevator pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a hydraulic press which from a first glance doesn’t seem that weird. It seems like just the ordinary hydraulic press located in different factories across the world. But upon further notice, you see that it contains several patches of skin with tattoos on them. To make things even weirder you notice that the skin doesn't match a specific skin tone (it differs from white to black skin tones). You come closer to the press and you're fascinated by the different tattoos displayed on its metalic frame. But then all the sudden…….

The machine transforms into a metalic cat like being with several blades coming from its body. The being moves closer at a fast speed and then all of the sudden one of its blades rips the tattooed flesh from your body with surgeon like skills. As you bleed your vision becomes blur. It gets blurrier and blurrier and just before you pass out, you see the being transform back into the hydraulic press. You see it pulvarize the flesh it took and then all the sudden your tattoo seems to appear on its metalic frame. Suddenly everything is dark and you're no more. But a part of you is now part of SCP-XXXX.

Central narrative:
A part of the SCP file is dedicated to the retrieval of SCP-XXXX. One of the researchers of SCP-XXXX interviews Agent Ford who helped to retrieve the SCP. During this interview we learn about the circumstances in which SCP-XXXX has been found and contained.
Example:
In 1988 several people went missing from a small town named Lockhart in Texas. A anonymous phone call from a women got the police to believe that the missing people were held at the Johnson & son factory in town. After some searching the officers and a foundation agent named Ford found a pile of dead bodies, their tattooed flesh ripped from their bodies. And next to it SCP-XXXX (the tattooed hydraulic press).

After the retrieval of SCP-XXXX the reader gets to read about research performed on SCP-XXXX. The reader learns about the nature of SCP-XXXX’s anomylous abilities. For example: SCP-XXXX has two modes of existence. It has its hydraulic press body which have several tattooed flesh patches on its frame, and it also has a secondary body, which is a cat like being into which the tattooed press transforms.

The research leads to several incidents and eventually to adjustments to the special containment procedures performed. While research is also starting to search for a way to use SCP-XXXX for the retrieval of other SCP's.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional.

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout.

Elevator Pitch: A broken man is stuck in his own hell, a 86 minute movie starring him, but something else is under the surface.

+ Central Narrative:
- Hide Central Narrative:

Bryce Cromwell was an average man, he never saw anything supernatural and worked a normal 9 to 5. But one day, he had been diagnosed with Alzheimer's and this changed his world forever. Words began to slip from his mind, things that should be there just weren't, and the only thing that forever was there was alcohol. And so he drank, he drank his worries, his mind away. He drank so much he didn't even remember his daughter or his wife, the only things that brought joy into this dark world. One night he drank too much, so much he forgot the pain of the crash, the crash that took his wife and daughter. After he woke up he was more sober than usual and could remember everything except the crash, he was horrified to see his wife and daughter's dead body in the trunk of his car. He wept for hours until he felt a presence behind him. A woman appeared, what he didn't know was that the woman was the titan Mnemosyne, the titan of memories. She proclaimed his sins and cursed him with the worst of fates, and so he was stuck in a cassette tape which held a 86 minute movie which when played would split his mind apart, one side when never played with his memories intact yet no concept of time, and his awake half which couldn't remember yet knew what time was. And so he was stuck for years like that until the foundation found him.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fear of what is inescapable, forgetting all that you learned and just how destructive our choices and what we can't control truly are.

Additional Notes: Second SCP, give me all you got.

item.title: SCP Idea: My Eyes are Up Here
item.content:encoded:
Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy/Horror(?)

Elevator Pitch: SCP researchers discover that after staring at the chest area of one of their female co-workers for over ten seconds, the word "M I N E" seems to appear on it etched in blood, changing the observer's eye color to an alarming shade of magenta and causing blindness if they continue staring.

Central Narrative: People frequently wondered why Dr. Jenna Lopez never seemed to mind that Dr. Briggs kept staring at her chest. Strangely, if anyone mentioned his ogling, both doctors would deny that he was ever looking, both appearing confused by the suggestion that such an event had ever occurred, until the events of August 9th, 2020. That day, at lunch in the cafeteria, Dr. Briggs was "enjoying the view", when suddenly, he started screaming. Co-workers turned to him, only to find that his irises had turned a viciously-bright shade of magenta. He, in a panicked frenzy, claimed that this was the first time he had ever looked at her chest, then vehemently insisted that he'd seen the word "M I N E" appear on her as if carved into the exposed skin. Other researchers, including Dr. Lopez herself, glanced down, only to see nothing of the sort. Briggs tried to insist again, continuing to look at her as the security team was called, only for him to start screaming again, this time out of intense pain rather than shock. Briggs then went fully blind. Lopez was temporarily confined, and tests started being performed.

Note: Lopez seems to completely lack control or intention regarding these effects, such that SCP-XXXX is identified as solely her chest, rather than the woman herself.

Containment: Since only exposed skin seems to cause the effects described, Lopez is allowed to roam free so long as she continues to wear clothing that covers her bosom (as well as an SCP-commissioned undergarment to prevent the effects from seeping through non-opaque fabrics). The classification is, for the time being, safe.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: First, the humor and righteousness of an SCP that punishes perverts who stare at this poor woman's chest. Second, the idea and potential ethical debate of an SCP attached to a non-SCP human person.
